summary: The International Monetary Fund, founded in 1945, appears in this atlas as one of the external constraints on Portuguese economic policy. Its stabilisation programmes framed the response to the balance-of-payments crises of 1977 and 1983 that followed the revolution and the oil shocks, and it returned in 2011 as one of the three institutions — with the European Commission and the European Central Bank — behind the adjustment programme. It is in the atlas because twice, a generation apart, the terms of Portuguese fiscal policy were written with it at the table.
